category: financial news API (REST, WebSocket and webhooks; sentiment and entity enrichment on paid plans)

free_tier.stated: Launchpad plan USD 0 per month: 5,000 requests per month, articles after a 12-hour delay, REST only, Discord support; webhook registration, ticker and entity data, sentiment analysis and WebSocket streams are not included.
free_tier.notes: Each REST request consumes one request from the monthly allowance, which resets at the start of the billing period. The Free plan covers roughly the last month of articles. A short-term burst limit per 10 seconds is enforced only on plans that define one. The next plan up is Pro Light at USD 29 a month with 10k requests per month; prices exclude applicable taxes.

retention.stated: roughly the last month of articles on the Free plan; requests for dates outside the window return no results
retention.notes: A query API with no stored objects.

egress.terms: not metered in bytes; the 5,000 requests a month bound what a free key can pull

interface_detail: POST https://api.finlight.me/v2/articles with an X-API-KEY header and a JSON body such as {"query": "Nvidia"}; WebSocket streams and webhooks are paid features. An MCP server at https://mcp.finlight.me is available on all plans, signs in with OAuth 2.0 and counts toward the same monthly quota.
tooling: any HTTP client; official client libraries for eight languages; an MCP server
chaining: A news feed delayed 12 hours over the last month at 5,000 requests a month, without sentiment or entity data on the Free plan, so a free stack pairs it with the GDELT event dataset for volume and a quote feed for prices.

limits.value: 5,000 requests per month on the Free plan; over it the API answers HTTP 429 until the next billing period
unverified: a burst limit per 10 seconds is enforced only on plans that define one, and the Free value is not published

limits_note: Plan gating: Free is REST only with no sentiment, ticker or entity data, webhooks or WebSocket streams; a request for a capability outside the plan answers HTTP 403. Bulk path: none; 100 articles per call.
binding_note: 5,000 requests a month binds first; the burst limit, where a plan defines one, is not published for Free.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form takes a full name, an email and a password of at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number and a symbol, or Continue with Google, with a terms checkbox, and shows no card field. unverified: no first-party page states whether the free plan needs a card.

reliability_note: Past the monthly quota the API answers HTTP 429, which clears at the start of the billing period; a burst 429 should wait about 10 seconds; no Retry-After or rate-limit headers are sent; a missing key answers HTTP 401.
confidence_note: The plan, quota, delay and history window are read from the first-party pricing and documentation pages. The articles route takes POST only, so the keyless 401 is documented, not measured; a free key was not exercised, so the card requirement and the Free burst limit are unverified: behind a sign-up.
